newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $63.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00, feedlot sources said.
The bids were $1.00 lower than active sales Tuesday at $64.00. The Tuesday activity, along with Friday's brisk trade, put a big dent in this week's showlist, they said.
"Showlists are pretty close to being sold out," one Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.
Sales the remainder of the week were seen light, likely at $63.00, several feedlot sources said. Fed cattle were pressured by large supplies and weak beef prices, they said.
Sales Tuesday were estimated near 55,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week-to-date estimate to about 114,000, the sources said.
Kansas fed cattle sales Tuesday were estimated at 46,500 head, with weekly movement seen near 111,000, they said.

Fed cattle prices also were pressured by outlooks for expanded market-ready supplies into the summer as large numbers of cattle placed onto feedlots in the spring are ready to be sold, the feedlot sources said.
Beef prices were lower on large packer inventories and lighter-than-expected beef consumption, they said.
